newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil may leave Urucum out of CVRD sale.
newsitem.headline: Brazil may leave Urucum out of CVRD sale.

text.p: The Brazilian government may leave Urucum, a subsidiary with iron ore and manganese rights, out of the planned sale of mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD), an official said.

Luiz Carlos Mendonca de Barros, head of the National Development Bank (BNDES), told a Congress hearing the bank may suggest at a National Privatization Council (CND) meeting Thursday that Urucum be withdrawn from the sales prospectus.
Urucum has become the focus of some controversy over the past week.
Deputy Saulo Quieroz of Mato Grosso do Sul state said several court proceedings had been taken out against CVRD's ownership of Urucum, bought up some three years ago.
Mato Grosso do Sul and Mato Grosso states, the previous owners of Urucum, are alleged to have sold the company at too low a price.
"Some madman could try and take out an injunction against the privatization. It's a risk," Quieroz said.
The CVRD privatization process is due to kick off on April 29 with the sale of a 45 percent controlling stake of the company's voting shares.
Mendonca de Barros was testifying to the lower house hearing on the privatization.
